Let \(S_i=a_1+\cdots+a_i\) be the ordinary prefix sum, and let \(V_i\) be the value obtained after applying \(\circ\) from left to right through \(a_i\).

Define \(D_i\) to be the sum of the terms that were subtracted rather than added. Every operation either adds or subtracts the next term, so
\[
V_i=S_i-2D_i.
\]
Consequently,
\[
V_i\equiv S_i\pmod 2.
\]
Thus, when appending \(a_{i+1}\),

- if \(a_{i+1}\) is odd, it is always added;
- if \(a_{i+1}\) is even, it is subtracted exactly when \(S_i\) is odd.

At the end, \(S_n=12\), so
\[
V_n=12-2D_n.
\]
Therefore \(V_n=0\) exactly when
\[
D_n=6.
\]

Now let \(F(s,d)\) be the number of sequences with ordinary sum \(s\) whose subtracted terms have total \(d\). Only even terms can be subtracted, so only even \(d\) are needed. Initialize
\[
F(0,0)=1.
\]
When the last term is \(x\),

- odd \(x\): \(F(s-x,d)\);
- even \(x\) and \(s-x\) even: \(x\) is added, giving \(F(s-x,d)\);
- even \(x\) and \(s-x\) odd: \(x\) is subtracted, giving \(F(s-x,d-x)\).

Applying this recurrence gives the following table, omitting odd values of \(d\), which are all zero:
